cleanIntro:
This guide follows Krieghoff's K-80 & K-20 manual; check your variant against it. The book covers the K-80 and K-20 over/unders and never prints "K-80 ACS", so every step here is the book's general K-80/K-20 procedure, stated as generally as the book states it. The sections the book gives to the Parcours, Trap Special and Pro Sporter models, and the optional fittings it marks K-80 only, are not used here.

The gun comes apart in three pieces — forend, barrels, receiver-and-stock — in that order. ⚠ The barrels are rocked off the pivots, never levered, and grease on the pivots is part of putting it back together.

steps.title: ⛔ This guide follows the K-80 & K-20 manual — check your variant
steps.action: This guide follows Krieghoff's K-80 & K-20 manual, which does not print "K-80 ACS", so check your variant against it. Everything below is the book's general K-80/K-20 procedure. Start where the book's safety rules start: treat the gun as loaded until you have looked into both chambers yourself.
steps.prose: A gun on the bench is the one most often assumed empty.
steps.quote: Handle a gun as if it is loaded. EVERY GUN IS A LOADED GUN!
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — GUN SAFETY, printed p.6

steps.title: Safety on — S showing
steps.action: The K-80's safety is a sliding switch with a round push button in its centre. Press the button with your thumb and slide the switch to the rear; the letter S appears just above it. ⚠ Krieghoff lets this safety be locked off for clay competition — if yours has been, the slide will not secure the gun, and the book says to make it operative for all other shooting.
steps.prose: Know which version of the safety you are holding before you trust it.
steps.aside: Make the safety operative for ALL other shooting.
steps.quote: The safety is activated by pressing the button with the thumb and simultaneously sliding the safety switch to the rear to put the gun "on safe".
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SAFETY, printed p.13

steps.title: Open the top lever, empty both chambers
steps.action: Point the muzzles somewhere safe, push the top lever across and let the barrels drop open fully. Take out any shells, then look into both chambers. ⚠ The ejectors are sprung — a fired case will be thrown, so do this where you can see where it lands.
steps.prose: Two barrels, two chambers, two looks.
steps.quote: Store all firearms unloaded! Be absolutely certain that the chamber of every gun is empty.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — GUN SAFETY, printed p.8

steps.title: Forend off first
steps.action: Take the forend off before anything else. It is what holds the barrels to the receiver, and Krieghoff gives the strip as assembly in reverse — assembly ends with the forend, so the strip begins with it.
steps.prose: The order is not optional on a break gun.
steps.quote: Disassemble the gun in the reverse order. Remove the forend.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.10

steps.title: Barrels off the pivots — rock, never pry
steps.action: Open the top lever and take the barrels off by gently rocking and rotating them until they come free of the pivots.
steps.prose: ⚠ This is the step that marks guns. One firm pull scars the bottom barrel or the receiver, and Krieghoff says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Then open the top lever and carefully remove the barrels by gently rocking and rotating them until they are disengaged from the pivots.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.10
steps.warn: Do not attempt to pry them off with a single motion because this may damage the finish of the bottom barrel or the receiver.

steps.title: Stock off only if you need it — through the recoil pad
steps.action: If the stock has to come off, put the supplied T-handled stock wrench through the small hole in the recoil pad and unscrew the stock bolt 2–3 turns. If it is tight, lay the receiver on a flat padded surface and gently bump the wrench handle or the bottom of the pistol grip with your palm. Make sure the bolt is fully disengaged, then draw the stock straight back.
steps.prose: Straight back, every time — this is inletted wood.
steps.quote: Make certain that the bolt is completely disengaged and then carefully remove the stock to the rear.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK REMOVAL AND REINSTALLATION — REMOVAL, printed p.11
steps.warn: Do not move the stock up and down to loosen and remove it because this may damage the inletting.

steps.title: ⛔ The butt plate is not in this book — Krieghoff puts it in another one
steps.action: If you came here to adjust an adjustable butt plate, stop: this manual does not carry those settings. Krieghoff publishes them in a separate instruction manual on its website. Nothing in this guide covers moving the plate, and nothing here should be used as if it did.
steps.prose: On a fitted clay gun the butt plate is the adjustment an owner reaches for most, which is why the boundary is stated rather than left to be discovered.
steps.quote: Please find a detailed description regarding the different settings of the butt plate in a separate instruction manual under:
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — ADJUSTABLE BUTT PLATE, printed p.30

steps.title: ⛔ That is the strip — springs and firing pins are factory work
steps.action: Forend, barrels, receiver-and-stock. The book publishes no owner strip of the receiver: the deepest thing it hands the owner is the ejectors (in Deep Clean). Replacing springs and firing pins and tuning the receiver is the work it assigns to Krieghoff's Annual Service. ⛔ Nothing past this point is in the book, and nothing past it is in this guide.
steps.prose: Three parts on the bench is the whole job.
steps.quote: The gun is disassembled, cleaned, and relubricated. Critical springs and firing pins are replaced and the receiver is fine tuned to original factory specifications.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE — ANNUAL SERVICE, printed p.36

deepSteps.title: Bores — solvent patches, bronze brush if you must
deepSteps.action: Clean the bores after shooting to take out lead fouling and wad plastic. Saturate patches with a conventional bore solvent and run them through on a shotgun cleaning rod; for stubborn fouling, more solvent and a phosphor bronze brush.
deepSteps.prose: Krieghoff's line is that bore and action get cleaned after every session.
deepSteps.aside: For particularly stubborn fouling, apply more solvent and use a phosphor bronze cleaning brush.
deepSteps.quote: The barrels must be cleaned after shooting to remove lead fouling and build up of plastic from wads.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.35

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes — only if your barrels take them
deepSteps.action: If your barrels have screw-in choke tubes, clean the bores first WITH the tubes in, then take the tubes out and clean them. Unload before a tube is touched. ⛔ A barrel built for choke tubes is never fired without one fitted.
deepSteps.prose: Chokes left in for months can rust into the barrel; the book says to take them out whenever the gun is cleaned.
deepSteps.aside: Choke tubes should be removed and cleaned whenever the gun is cleaned.
deepSteps.quote: If your barrel is equipped with choke tubes, clean the barrel first with the tubes installed and then remove and clean the tubes themselves as described before.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.35
deepSteps.warn: Never shoot a choke tubed barrel without a choke tube installed.

deepSteps.title: Choke threads clean, choke lube, in by hand
deepSteps.action: Solvent on the tube, wiped clean, with particular attention to the threads; solvent on the threads inside the barrel too, wiped clean. A light coat of Krieghoff Choke Lube or another choke-tube grease goes on before the tube goes back. Screw it in by hand — any roughness means something is dirty, dry or damaged — then snug it gently with the choke wrench.
deepSteps.prose: A choke that will not turn by hand is telling you to stop.
deepSteps.aside: Install the choke tube by hand.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a light coat of Krieghoff Choke Lube or other choke tube grease to the choke tube before reinstalling it in the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SCREW-IN CHOKES, printed p.20
deepSteps.warn: Never apply force when installing a choke tube and never over tighten.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Look through the bore after every choke change
deepSteps.action: Every time a tube goes in, look down the bore and make sure it does not stand into the barrel anywhere. A dented tube can protrude, and Krieghoff warns the barrel can be destroyed when it is fired. ⛔ A damaged tube is thrown away, not used.
deepSteps.prose: A dropped choke gets inspected before it gets fitted.
deepSteps.quote: Whenever you change or reinstall choke tubes, look through the bore to make absolutely certain that the tube does not protrude into or obstruct the barrel in any way.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SCREW-IN CHOKES, printed p.20
deepSteps.warn: NEVER shoot with a damaged choke tube.

deepSteps.title: Ejectors out — one at a time, over a towel
deepSteps.action: The ejectors may come out for periodic cleaning. Unload first, and work over a flat surface covered with a towel. Push both ejectors back gently until you feel resistance, then tap very lightly with a plastic mallet until it goes. Keep a thumb over the detent area, hold the barrels horizontal close to the covered table with the ejector to be removed facing down, and slide it out to the rear — the ball pops out onto the towel. Set the ball aside and lift the spring out with tweezers. ⚠ The ejectors are fitted to each side: do one at a time.
deepSteps.prose: The towel is there to catch a ball bearing you will not find on a hard floor.
deepSteps.aside: Remove the ejector and set the ball aside.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the spring with a pair of tweezers.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING, CLEANING AND REINSTALLING EJECTORS — REMOVAL, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Ejector and groove — cleaned, then a light coat of oil
deepSteps.action: Clean the ejector and its groove with a fine-quality cleaner; a small brush takes stubborn debris off the ejector. Spray cleaner into the groove and wipe it out — a pipe cleaner or cotton swab gets what is left. Wipe the groove clean, then give the ejector and the groove a light coat of gun oil before it goes back.
deepSteps.prose: Dirt in the groove is what makes an ejector stick.
deepSteps.quote: like Krieghoff's Gun Pro, and reinstall the ejector.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING, CLEANING AND REINSTALLING EJECTORS — CLEANING, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Ejector back in — listen for the click
deepSteps.action: Spring into its hole. Ejector into the groove on its own side — the machined recess on its front outside opens downward when it is right — and pushed in until its front end is even with the hole. A small dab of oil on the spring, the ball on top, then press the ball down with a small flat screwdriver while sliding the ejector forward to partly cover the hole. Take the tool away and slide the ejector the rest of the way. It is seated when the spring pushes the ball into the detent with an audible click. Slide it back and forth to check, then do the other side.
deepSteps.quote: Place the spring in the hole.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING, CLEANING AND REINSTALLING EJECTORS — REINSTALLATION, printed p.32

deepSteps.title: Bearing surfaces — old grease off, fresh grease on
deepSteps.action: With the gun apart, wipe the bearing surfaces clean of old grease and the grit picked up shooting. Then make sure the barrel pivots, barrel ears and forearm iron all carry enough grease, and keep dirt off them. ⛔ Whatever you clean with, Krieghoff limits it to acid- and resin-free detergents.
deepSteps.prose: Grit in grease is lapping compound.
deepSteps.quote: Be sure that all bearing surfaces have sufficient grease, including the barrel pivots, barrel ears and forearm iron.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.35
deepSteps.warn: Use only acid- and resign-free detergents for cleaning!

deepSteps.title: Solvent out, thin oil in, mainsprings eased
deepSteps.action: No solvent stays in the gun — all of it comes out. For storage, a very thin film of good gun oil goes into chamber and bore. When you are done, Krieghoff recommends taking the tension off the mainsprings by dry-firing on snap caps.
deepSteps.aside: When finished cleaning, we recommend relieving the tension on the mainsprings by dry firing with snap caps.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure, that after cleaning, no solvent is left in the gun.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.35

deepSteps.title: Wet gun — apart, dried separately, then oiled
deepSteps.action: If the gun gets wet, wipe down the stock, forend, receiver and barrels and let them air-dry separately. Once the metal is completely dry, give it a light coat of gun oil. Straight after any session, before it goes in the case, the outside metal is wiped down and lightly oiled.
deepSteps.prose: A wet gun closed in a case is a rusty gun in a week.
deepSteps.aside: Immediately after shooting and before casing, the gun's external metal surfaces should be wiped down and oiled lightly.
deepSteps.quote: If your gun does get wet, however, the stock, forend, receiver, and barrels should be wiped down and allowed to air dry separately.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL K-80 & K-20 — Handling and Service Instructions for the Krieghoff K-80 and K-20 Over/Under Shotguns. — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK FINISH, printed p.26

cleaning.name: BARRELS AND CHOKES
tasks: Bores cleaned of lead and wad plastic — solvent patches, phosphor bronze brush for stubborn fouling
Choke-tube barrels: bore cleaned with tubes in, then tubes out and cleaned
Tube and barrel threads wiped clean; light coat of choke lube before the tube goes back in by hand
⛔ Never fire a choke-tubed barrel with no tube fitted
Bore looked through after every choke change
No solvent left behind; very thin film of oil in chamber and bore for storage

cleaning.name: EJECTORS
tasks: Removed one at a time, over a towel
Ejector and groove cleaned, then lightly oiled
Reseated with an audible click and slid back and forth to check

cleaning.name: ACTION AND STOCK
tasks: Bearing surfaces wiped of old grease and grit
Thin grease in the barrel pivots; very light coat on the flats beside them, the barrel lug, the barrel flats and the forend iron
Do not clean with acidic or resinous detergents
External metal wiped and lightly oiled before casing
Mainsprings eased on snap caps when finished

reassembly: Pivots greased first — a thin coat in the barrel pivots, a very light coat on the flats, lug, barrel flats and forend iron.
Both ejectors pushed in, top lever open.
Barrels engaged at about 45°, rocked up and down onto the pivots, rotated slightly to confirm they are seated, then the gun closed fully.
Cocking levers pushed up parallel to the barrels; forend slots engaged on them; forend pressed up until the latch fully engages.
⚠ Keep the forend iron's sharp edges off the underside of the barrels and the receiver.
Stock (if removed) slid straight on and the bolt tightened firmly but not excessively — never forced or rocked.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed empty, close it and check that the top lever has gone across and the barrels are locked. Work the safety: button pressed and slid back, S showing; slid forward, S covered. With the action OPEN, move the barrel selector to B and to T — Krieghoff advises operating the selector with the action open. Then ease the mainsprings on snap caps, as the book recommends after cleaning.
